title: Hironaka near-point additive symmetry of the normal-cone equations
statement:
Let $F$ be a field of any characteristic and let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero reduced Noetherian local commutative $F$-algebra essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be a prime ideal, assume $A=R/I$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme], and assume that no minimal prime of $R$ contains $I$ (a minimal prime is a prime ideal containing no strictly smaller prime). Put $k=R/\mathfrak m$ and $S=(\operatorname{gr}_I R)\otimes_A k$, and assume $\operatorname{gr}_I R$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $Y=\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}R)$ and let $y\in Y$ lie over the closed point [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-nagata-affine-blowup]. Identify this fibre with $\operatorname{Proj}S$ [def-pc-proj]. Set $R_y=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n_y$, and set
$$h_R(n)=\operatorname{length}_R(R/\mathfrak m^{n+1}),\quad h_y(n)=\operatorname{length}_{R_y}(R_y/\mathfrak n_y^{n+1}),\quad \delta=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(y)$$
[def-weil-pbc-module-length, def-kun-transcendence-degree, def-weil-residue-field], and $\Lambda f(n)=\sum_{j=0}^n f(j)$. Assume $\Lambda^\delta h_y=h_R$.
For any graded surjection $P=k[Z_1,\ldots,Z_N]\twoheadrightarrow S$, with variables of degree one, let $K$ be its homogeneous kernel and let $\mathfrak q_y\subset P$ be the inverse image of the homogeneous prime representing $y$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. There exists a proper homogeneous ideal $L\subseteq\mathfrak q_y$ such that, in polynomial rings on disjoint variable tuples $Z,W$,
$$f(0)=0,\quad f(-Z)\in L(Z),\quad f(Z+W)\in L(Z)+L(W)\quad(f\in L),$$
$$g(Z+W)\in K(Z)+L(W)\quad(g\in K).$$
Here $L(Z)$, $L(W)$ and $K(Z)$ mean the ideals generated by the indicated substitutions in the larger polynomial ring. Thus the assertion records the equations of a homogeneous additive subgroup and its translation action on the normal-cone fibre; it does not assert that $L$ is generated in degree one.

source.place: VIII 2.3.13, printed p.94, synchronization motivation only. Precise source read online: Cossart--Jannsen--Saito, March 12 2009 preprint, Theorem 2.10(2), printed pp.32--33, and the characteristic-independent additive-subgroup argument in the proof of Theorem 2.14, printed p.36, before its linearity argument: Hironaka [H4], Certain numerical characters of singularities, Theorem IV, and [H5], Additive groups associated with points of a projective space, Theorem 2. The normal-cone quotient used there is Theorem 2.2(2)(ii), printed p.28.; https://epub.uni-regensburg.de/13766/1/MP32.pdf. Archival copy and cited originals WANTED; no Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Apply lem-trf-near-point-order-presentation to the canonical point ideal q=phi^(-1)(nearPointFibreIdeal). It supplies N>=1, a homogeneous relevant prime q, and K generated by homogeneous positive-degree elements whose local order at q is at least their degree. This encapsulates the original minimal-presentation reduction and local fraction-map transfer, without any additive-symmetry conclusion.

Apply lem-trf-projective-order-algebra-additive-generators to q. Write its algebra U as k[T] for its positive-degree homogeneous additive generators T. Each homogeneous order generator H of K lies in U: its component in its own degree is H, all other components are zero. By the two span inclusions, K=span(K intersection U). Each t in T has positive local order, so its localized image is in qP_q. The local maximal-ideal membership criterion gives t in q.

Set L=Ideal.span T. Ideal.homogeneous_span proves homogeneity. Since T is contained in q, L is contained in q and proper. Positive-degree homogeneity forces the constant coefficient of each generator to vanish. The kernel of evaluation at zero is an ideal containing T, so it contains L.

Let z,w denote the two renamings and a the addition substitution. Substitute (Z,-Z) into a(t)=z(t)+w(t); the zero constant coefficient gives neg(t)=-z(t). The inverse images under inversion and addition of L(Z) and L(Z)+L(W) are ideals containing T. The span universal property therefore gives both memberships for all f in L.

Take the quotient by D=L(W). The two k-algebra maps from P to P[W]/D, addition followed by quotient and z followed by quotient, agree on T. AlgHom.adjoin_le_equalizer extends this equality to k[T]=U. Thus a(g)-z(g) belongs to D for every g in U. When g also belongs to K, z(g) lies in K(Z), hence a(g) lies in K(Z)+D. Its inverse image under a is an ideal containing K intersection U; because K=span(K intersection U), it contains all of K. This is the final translation-action clause. All computations are polynomial identities and work in every characteristic.

proof_origin.place: Original six-step additive-subgroup argument (Hironaka/Dietel/CJS references retained). Steps 1--3 numerical presentation comparison split into lem-trf-near-point-order-presentation; explicit Lean proof of steps 4--6 using span and algebra equalizer universal properties.

The item is not on the drop list and is unsplit in live and side-live; its statement is unchanged; there is no SGA. Source check (I read Dietel 2014 pp.107-110 myself): (1) lem-trf-projective-order-algebra-additive-generators is Dietel Lemma 9.1.4 (Giraud III 2.2.4, Hironaka H5).
